subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these exact pinned third-party action revisions in workflows that use GitHub App keys, registry credentials, and OpenAI API keys?
rationale: This is a trust and privilege-boundary choice: source review can identify the affected secret-bearing workflows but cannot authorize new upstream action code on the repository’s behalf.

options.title: Approve reviewed revisions
options.body: A workflow-security owner reviews the upstream SHAs and accepts them after current-head workflow evidence confirms the affected paths remain safe.

options.title: Split sensitive updates
options.body: Land only action updates outside credential-bearing workflows and defer GitHub App-token, registry-login, and Codex-action revisions for separate security review.

options.title: Pause this aggregate bump
options.body: Close or supersede this broad Dependabot update and refresh a narrower dependency PR after the workflow trust decision is documented.

recommendation.title: Approve reviewed revisions
recommendation.body: A workflow-security owner reviews the upstream SHAs and accepts them after current-head workflow evidence confirms the affected paths remain safe.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository’s official contributing guidance names @steipete as the primary project-level decision owner; workflow-specific history could not be read in this restricted environment.
